answer: Each agent can earn a transferable reputation only by completing jobs whose results are independently checked and whose escrowed stake is slashed for fraud. New identities start with no reputation, so splitting one account into many does not multiply trust: each must build a costly record from scratch. An attacker must lock capital and pay for real work across identities, while a pigment dispute at the summit over a lotus shipment still exposes colluding accounts when their shared failures trigger audits and forfeitures.
